neighbours.label: a word introducing how an action is done (through, as though, using, following) right after the verb phrase
fire: In the meantime, she views the world through the lens of her old camera.
It is unhelpful to describe the right as though it needed only one duty.
The system works using a principle known as field evaporation.
He spoke to the crowd as if nothing had happened that morning.
The colour is described following three simple criteria.
We sent the files through a secure server overnight.
She treated the puppy as though it were a small child.
The engineers cut the steel using a high-pressure water jet.
quiet: In the meantime, she keeps her old camera in a drawer at home.
It is unhelpful to describe the right in such vague terms.
The system was installed last year in the main laboratory.
He spoke to the crowd for nearly an hour that morning.
The colour is described in the second chapter of the report.
We sent the files to the office overnight.
She treated the puppy to a long walk in the park.
The engineers cut the steel into three equal pieces.

notes: card: ' through' x4, ' though' (as though), ' if' (as if), ' used', Spanish 'siguiendo', Russian 'используя'. Near misses end the verb phrase without a manner/means connective.
